families.description: This domain contains several highly conserved charged amino acids, suggesting this may be an enzymatic domain (Bateman A pers. obs). The entry includes SanA [swissprot:P33017] and Sfix ([swissprot:O33790]) from Salmonella typhimurium which are involved in Vancomycin resistance [[cite:PUB00019464]]. These proteins may be involved in murein synthesis [[cite:PUB00019465]]. This domain is found in Escherichia coli YdcF, which has been shown to bind S-adenosyl-L-methionine (AdoMet), but whose biochemical function has not been identified [[cite:PUB00050945]].

It shows a cone-like alpha+beta barrel structure with a long N-terminal alpha- helix, a curved six-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and two additional shorter alpha-helices. Its specific function is still unkown [[cite:PUB00100883]].

families.description: This family includes the DUF34/metal-binding protein/NIF3 proteins, which are widely distributed across superkingdoms. They were previously annotated as GTP cyclohydrolase 1 type 2 [[cite:PUB00070175]] and, recently, through a comprehensive literature review and integrative bioinformatics analyses it was revealed that annotations for these members were misleading as they were based on a single set of in vitro results examining the NIF3 homolog of Helicobacter pylori [[cite:PUB00070175]]. Actually, they have varied phenotypes with the unifying functional role as metal-binding proteins [[cite:PUB00100327]]. This entry contains several NIF3 (NGG1p interacting factor 3) protein homologues. NIF3 interacts with the yeast transcriptional coactivator NGG1p which is part of the ADA complex, the exact function of this interaction is unknown [[cite:PUB00002954],[cite:PUB00019927]].
families.name: Duf34/NIF3 (NGG1p interacting factor 3)

families.description: Members of this family have so far been found in bacteria and mouse SwissProt or TrEMBL entries. However possible family members have also been identified in translated rat (Genbank:AW144450) and human (Genbank:AI478629) ESTs. A mouse family member has been named SIMPL (signalling molecule that associates with mouse pelle-like kinase). SIMPL appears to facilitate and/or regulate complex formation between IRAK/mPLK (IL-1 receptor-associated kinase) and IKK (inhibitor of kappa-B kinase) containing complexes, and thus regulate NF-kappa-B activity [[cite:PUB00010115]]. Separate experiments demonstrate that a mouse family member (named LaXp180) binds the Listeria monocytogenes surface protein ActA, which is a virulence factor that induces actin polymerisation. It may also bind stathmin, a protein involved in signal transduction and in the regulation of microtubule dynamics [[cite:PUB00009982]]. In bacteria its function is unknown, but it is thought to be located in the periplasm or outer membrane.
families.name: Protein of unknown function (DUF541)

families.description: This an all-beta structure with a twenty-residue repeat with a highly conserved repeating GD, gly-asp, motif that has been described as Toastrack DUF4097, whose function is unknown. It has been suggested to form part of a bacterial adhesin. Toastrack has been transferred from bacteria to certain eukaryotes, such as FAM185A from human and its orthologues in animals and other eukaryotes.

It associates with microtubules and recruits TON1A and TON1B to the cytoskeleton through its C-terminal [[cite:PUB00078481],[cite:PUB00095561]].

families.description: The apaG domain is a ~125 amino acids domain present in bacterial apaG proteins and in eukaryotic F-box proteins. The domain is named after the bacterial apaG protein, of which it forms the core. The domain also occurs in the C-terminal part of eukaryotic proteins with an N-terminal F-box domain. The Salmonella typhimurium apaG domain protein corD is involved in Co(2+) resistance and Mg(2+) efflux. Tertiary structures from different apaG proteins show a fold of several beta-sheets. The apaG domain may be involved in protein-protein interactions which could be implicated in substrate-specificity [[cite:PUB00009972],[cite:PUB00016988],[cite:PUB00018539],[cite:PUB00016989]].
families.name: ApaG domain

families.description: This entry represents the central domain found in archaeal proteins such as DNA double-strand break repair helicase HerA ([ec:3.6.4.12]). HerA is a helicase which is able to utilise either 3' or 5' single-stranded DNA extensions for loading and subsequent DNA duplex unwinding [[cite:PUB00076694]]. It forms a complex with NurA nuclease, this complex has the 5'-3' DNA end resection activity and is essential for cell viability in the crenarchaeon Sulfolobus islandicus [[cite:PUB00076695]]. This domain includes the the central RecA-like catalytic core and a flanking four-helix bundle [[cite:PUB00078094]]. The function of this prokaryotic domain is unknown. It contains several conserved aspartates and histidines that could be metal ligands.
families.name: Helicase HerA, central domain

families.description: This bacterial family of proteins shows structural similarity to other pectin lyase families. Although structures from this family align with acetyl-transferases, there is no conservation of catalytic residues found. It is likely that the function is one of cell-adhesion. In PDB:3jx8, it is interesting to note that the sequence of contains several well defined sequence repeats, centred around GSG motifs defining the tight beta turn between the two sheets of the super-helix; there are 8 such repeats in the C-terminal half of the protein, which could be grouped into 4 repeats of two. It seems likely that this family belongs to the superfamily of trimeric auto-transporter adhesins (TAAs), which are important virulence factors in Gram-negative pathogens [[cite:PUB00029784]] [[cite:PUB00051306]]. In the case of Parabacteroides distasonis, which is a component of the normal distal human gut microbiota, TAA-like complexes probably modulate adherence to the host (information derived from TOPSAN).
families.name: Putative auto-transporter adhesin, head GIN domain

families.description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

QueG catalyses the conversion of epoxyqueuosine (oQ) to queuosine (Q), which is a hypermodified base found in the wobble positions of tRNA(Asp), tRNA(Asn), tRNA(His) and tRNA(Tyr) [[cite:PUB00058202]].
families.name: Epoxyqueuosine reductase QueG, DUF1730

families.description: These proteins are related to the [pfam:PF00462] family. This entry includes several viral glutaredoxins and many related bacterial and eukaryotic proteins of unknown function. The best characterised member is G4L ([swissprot:P68460]) from Vaccinia virus (strain Western Reserve/WR) (VACV), which is necessary for virion morphogenesis and replication [[cite:PUB00020627]]. This is a cytoplasmic protein which functions as a shuttle in a redox pathway between membrane-associated E10R and L1R or F9L [[cite:PUB00020628]].

The domain represented by this entry has significant to known winged helix domains.

Many of these proteins are annotated as multidrug ABC transporters or ABC-2 type transport systems, including some daunorubicin/doxorubicin resistance proteins. This family is found almost exclusively in Actinomycetota, particularly Streptomyces. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

families.description: Family member FomD is a protein encoded in the fosfomycin biosynthesis gene cluster [[cite:PUB00009885],[cite:PUB00100530]], which hydrolyses (S)-HPP-CMP to give (S)-HPP and CMP in the presence of Mn2 or Co2 [[cite:PUB00100530]]. FomD also hydrolyses cytidylyl 2-hydroxyethylphosphonate (HEP-CMP), which is a biosynthetic intermediate before C-methylation. FomD structure revealed that it has a beta-barrel fold consisting of a large twisted antiparallel beta-sheet, a key feature of DUF402-containing proteins. The function of this domain is unknown. It has a Tyr residue which activates a water molecule to promote nucleophilic attack on the phosphorus atom of the phosphonate moiety [[cite:PUB00100530]]. This domain has also been found in Ntdp (nucleoside tri- and diphosphatase, also known as Sa1684) from Staphylococcus aureus [[cite:PUB00100531]].

families.description: Two structures have been solved for members of this large (>500 members) family of bacterial proteins present mostly in environmental bacteria and metagenomes (distant homologues are also present in several Plasmodium species). TOPSAN analysis for pdb:3pjy shows that there is much similarity with the other solved structure, pdb:3m7a, solved for UniProt:Q2GA55 (Saro_0823), a homologue of Thermotoga maritima TM1668, UniProt:Q9X1Z6., The homologue in Caulobacter crescentus (CC1388), UniProt:Q9A8G6, is associated with CspD, a cold shock protein (CC1387), UniProt:Q9A8G7. However, the genomic context of UniProt:Q2GA55 is most conserved with a putative xylose isomerase, suggesting a possible role in extracellular sugar processing. Saro_0821, UniProt:Q2GA57, is annotated as an AMP-dependent synthetase and ligase. PDB:3m7a structure corresponds to the C-terminal (27-165) fragment of the YP_496102 (Saro_0823) protein and it is structurally unique, as the best hits from Dali have a Z-score of 3.8 (1nt0, 2j1t, 3kq4) and it is thus a likely candidate for a new fold. Interestingly, many of the top Dali hits are involved in sugar metabolism. There are no obvious active site-like cavities on the protein surface of 3m7a (http://www.topsan.org/Proteins/JCSG/).

families.description: This is a bacterial family of putative lipoproteins. The structure for [swissprot:Q64U78], PDB:3fzx, the first structural template for this large family including several homologues in the human gut microbiome and in metagenomic datasets, folds into a beta barrel that topologically looks like a small-scale porin (such as FepA). [swissprot:Q64U78] is a putative exported protein, and this fold is of the YmcC-like type, with a predicted signal peptide SpI cleavage site AGAMA|QNQDC, and a Phobius server prediction of non-cytoplasmic localisation for amino acids 21-236. The possibility of it being a membrane protein can be ruled out by the hydrophilic nature of the solvent exposed surface outside the barrels. Analysis of sequence conservation suggests that an area near Glu172/Trp206 is potentially interesting. These two residues are also conserved in Dali hit PDB:2in5, a hypothetical lipoprotein classified as a new YmcC-like fold in SCOP (SCOP:159271, with a 12-stranded meander beta-sheet folded into a deformed beta-barrel) despite large structural differences between the two structures, suggesting similarity in function.

BDCPs are associated with lysosome size, apoptosis, autophagy, granule size, or synapse formation. Mutations in this domain have been related to autosomal recessively inherited lipopolysaccharide-responsive beige-like anchor (LRBA) protein deficiency, responsible for common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) and autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) [[cite:PUB00098183]]. NBEAs deficiency may induce spine loss with defects in synaptic efficacy and plasticity, being associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and ASD-related syndromes [[cite:PUB00098182]].

The bacterial proteins are likely to be involved in a cell wall function as they are found in conjunction with the [pfam:PF07501] domain, which is involved in various cell surface processes. This domain is also present in the resuscitation-promoting factors RpfB from Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Rpf2 from Corynebacterium glutamicum. These are factors that stimulate resuscitation of dormant cells [[cite:PUB00075582]]. This domain has a beta grasp fold. Structural description of this domain revealed a structural conservation between these domains and ubiquitin, hence it is termed UBL-G5 [[cite:PUB00137668]].

The AtDMP proteins are predicted to have four transmembrane spans, with cytosolic amino- and carboxy-termini. DMP1 is a membrane protein that may be involved in membrane fission during breakdown of the ER and the tonoplast during leaf senescence and in membrane fusion during vacuole biogenesis in roots [[cite:PUB00086645]]. Several DMP proteins are expressed in senescing organs (DMP1, -3, -4) or tissues that will stall later in development (DMP1, -2, -4, -7). These expression patterns strongly suggest involvement of several DMPs in various programmed cell death processes, e.g. senescence, dehiscence and abscission [[cite:PUB00136742]]. AtDMP8 and AtDMP9 however, have been shown to facilitate gamete fusion during double fertilisation in flowering plants [[cite:PUB00093467]].

Although function of this domain is currently unknown, studies on TCTN2 suggest that it is indispensable for its functions [[cite:PUB00097826],[cite:PUB00097827]]. TCTN1, TCTN2, and TCTN3 are members of the tectonic protein family that play crucial roles in ciliogenesis and ciliary function. While they share some common functions, each protein also has specific roles in the process of cilia formation and maintenance. These proteins interact with several other ciliopathy proteins, forming a complex known as the Tectonic ciliopathy complex. This complex is required for hedgehog signalling transduction and regulation of ciliary membrane composition [[cite:PUB00069722],[cite:PUB00160606]].

families.description: This entry represents a highly conserved 100 residue coiled-coil region which is found in short coiled-coil protein (SCOC) in human and UNC-69 in Caenorhabditis elegans. In human, SCOC is required for autophagosome formation during amino acid starvation. It forms a starvation-sensitive trimeric complex with UVRAG (UV radiation resistance associated gene) and FEZ1 and may regulate ULK1 and Beclin 1 complex activities [[cite:PUB00086016]]. In C. elegans, this small, evolutionarily conserved coiled-coil domain-containing protein, UNC-69, acts as a binding partner of UNC-76. Together they participate in a common genetic pathway necessary for axon extension and cooperate to regulate the size and position of synaptic vesicles in axons. Moreover, both proteins colocalize as puncta in neuronal processes and mutations in UNC-69 preferentially disrupt membrane traffic within axons [[cite:PUB00109243]].

families.description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and includes YfiR from E. coli. YfiR may serve as a periplasmic redox sensor that regulates YfiN activity in response to reducing conditions [[cite:PUB00088310],[cite:PUB00088309]]. HmsC is a periplasmic protein that interacts directly with the periplasmic domain (PD) of HmsD and causes proteolytic degradation of HmsD, which in turn negatively regulates Y. pestis biofilm formation [[cite:PUB00091014]].

The structure of UnioProtKB:B8FUJ5, PDB:3l5o, suggests that the protein has an enolase N-terminal-like fold and this Rossmann-like C-terminal domain. Solution of the structures of the two members of this family investigated bear some resemblance to that of the single domain enzyme pterin-4a-carbinolamine dehydratase, PDC. Although the residues of PCDs involved in binding of metabolite are not conserved in the two structures under study, they do correspond to a surface-region structurally aligned with residues that are highly conserved, eg Glu 89, suggesting that this region is also involved in binding of a ligand, thereby possibly constituting a catalytic site of a yet uncharacterised enzyme specific for gamma proteobacteria.

families.description: This bacterial family of proteins has no known function. However, the cis-regulatory yjdF motif, just upstream from the gene encoding the proteins for this family, is a small non-coding RNA, Rfam:RF01764. The yjdF motif is found in many Firmicutes, including Bacillus subtilis. In most cases, it resides in potential 5' UTRs of homologues of the yjdF gene whose function is unknown. However, in Streptococcus thermophilus, a yjdF RNA motif is associated with an operon whose protein products synthesise nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+). Also, the S. thermophilus yjdF RNA lacks typical yjdF motif consensus features downstream of and including the P4 stem. Thus, if yjdF RNAs are riboswitch aptamers, the S. thermophilus RNAs might sense a distinct compound that structurally resembles the ligand bound by other yjdF RNAs. On the ohter hand, perhaps these RNAs have an alternative solution forming a similar binding site, as is observed with some SAM riboswitches [[cite:PUB00109804]].

families.description: This group of 2H-phosphodiesterases comprises a single family typified by the protein mlr3352 from M.loti. Members are also present in various alpha-proteobacteria, Synechocystis, Streptococcus and Chilo iridescent virus. The presence of a member of this predominantly bacterial group in a large eukaryotic DNA virus represents a potential case of horizontal transfer from a bacterial source into a virus. Several proteins of bacterial origin have been noticed in the insect viruses (L.M.Iyer, E.V.Koonin and L.Aravind, unpublished observations and these appear to have been acquired from endo-symbiotic or parasitic bacteria that share the same host cells with the viruses. Presence of 2H proteins in the proteomes of large DNA viruses (e.g. T4 57B protein and the Fowl-pox virus FPV025) may point to some role for these proteins in regulating the viral tRNA metabolism. Each member of this family contains an internal duplication, each of which contains an HXTX motif that defines the family.

families.description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are probably remotely related to His-Me finger endonucleases. record.description: This family consists of various hypothetical proteins from cyanobacteria, none of which are functionally described. The aligned region is approximately 120-140 amino acids long corresponding to almost the entire length of the proteins in the family. [swissprot:Q2RPE2], PDB:3fcn, is a small protein that has a novel all-alpha fold. The N-terminal helical hairpin is likely to function as a dimerisation module. This protein is a member of PFam family PF01724. The function of this protein is unknown. One protein sequence contains a fusion of this protein and a DnaB domain, suggesting a possible role in DNA helicase activity (hypothetical). Dali hits have low Z and high rmsd, suggesting probably only topological similarities (not functional relevance) (details derived from TOPSAN). The family has several highly conserved sequence motifs, including YD/ExD, DxxNVxEEIE, and CPY/F/W, as well as conserved tryptophans.

record.description: This family includes the DUF34/metal-binding protein/NIF3 proteins, which are widely distributed across superkingdoms. They were previously annotated as GTP cyclohydrolase 1 type 2 [[cite:PUB00070175]] and, recently, through a comprehensive literature review and integrative bioinformatics analyses it was revealed that annotations for these members were misleading as they were based on a single set of in vitro results examining the NIF3 homolog of Helicobacter pylori [[cite:PUB00070175]]. Actually, they have varied phenotypes with the unifying functional role as metal-binding proteins [[cite:PUB00100327]]. This entry contains several NIF3 (NGG1p interacting factor 3) protein homologues. NIF3 interacts with the yeast transcriptional coactivator NGG1p which is part of the ADA complex, the exact function of this interaction is unknown [[cite:PUB00002954],[cite:PUB00019927]].
record.name: Duf34/NIF3 (NGG1p interacting factor 3)

The NMR structure of a DUF61 family member from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Sulfolobus solfataricus revealed a rigid core structure and flexible N- and C-terminal regions, including a negatively-charged independent C-terminal helix. The core structure consists of N- and C-terminal subdomains, in which the C-terminal subdomain shows significant structural similarity with several nucleic acid binding proteins [[cite:PUB00098020]].

record.description: This entry represents the central domain found in archaeal proteins such as DNA double-strand break repair helicase HerA ([ec:3.6.4.12]). It forms a complex with NurA nuclease, this complex has the 5'-3' DNA end resection activity and is essential for cell viability in the crenarchaeon Sulfolobus islandicus [[cite:PUB00076695]]. This domain includes the the central RecA-like catalytic core and a flanking four-helix bundle [[cite:PUB00078094]]. The function of this prokaryotic domain is unknown. It contains several conserved aspartates and histidines that could be metal ligands.

record.description: Two structures have been solved for members of this large (>500 members) family of bacterial proteins present mostly in environmental bacteria and metagenomes (distant homologues are also present in several Plasmodium species). TOPSAN analysis for pdb:3pjy shows that there is much similarity with the other solved structure, pdb:3m7a, solved for UniProt:Q2GA55 (Saro_0823), a homologue of Thermotoga maritima TM1668, UniProt:Q9X1Z6., The homologue in Caulobacter crescentus (CC1388), UniProt:Q9A8G6, is associated with CspD, a cold shock protein (CC1387), UniProt:Q9A8G7. However, the genomic context of UniProt:Q2GA55 is most conserved with a putative xylose isomerase, suggesting a possible role in extracellular sugar processing. Saro_0821, UniProt:Q2GA57, is annotated as an AMP-dependent synthetase and ligase. PDB:3m7a structure corresponds to the C-terminal (27-165) fragment of the YP_496102 (Saro_0823) protein and it is structurally unique, as the best hits from Dali have a Z-score of 3.8 (1nt0, 2j1t, 3kq4) and it is thus a likely candidate for a new fold. DMP1 is a membrane protein that may be involved in membrane fission during breakdown of the ER and the tonoplast during leaf senescence and in membrane fusion during vacuole biogenesis in roots [[cite:PUB00086645]]. Several DMP proteins are expressed in senescing organs (DMP1, -3, -4) or tissues that will stall later in development (DMP1, -2, -4, -7). These expression patterns strongly suggest involvement of several DMPs in various programmed cell death processes, e.g. senescence, dehiscence and abscission [[cite:PUB00136742]]. AtDMP8 and AtDMP9 however, have been shown to facilitate gamete fusion during double fertilisation in flowering plants [[cite:PUB00093467]].

record.description: This is a conserved domain found in tectonic proteins (TCTN1/2/3) which contains conserved cysteine residues predicted to form disulfide bond. This domain is found in two tandem copies. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure with unique topology composed of a central mixed beta-sheet and alpha-helix packed on it. Although function of this domain is currently unknown, studies on TCTN2 suggest that it is indispensable for its functions [[cite:PUB00097826],[cite:PUB00097827]]. TCTN1, TCTN2, and TCTN3 are members of the tectonic protein family that play crucial roles in ciliogenesis and ciliary function. While they share some common functions, each protein also has specific roles in the process of cilia formation and maintenance. These proteins interact with several other ciliopathy proteins, forming a complex known as the Tectonic ciliopathy complex. This complex is required for hedgehog signalling transduction and regulation of ciliary membrane composition [[cite:PUB00069722],[cite:PUB00160606]].

record.description: This domain of unknown function is found in O-mannosyl -transferases TMTC1-4, and constitutes a loop between TM7 and TM8 located in the ER lumen that contains a small hydrophobic, but not membrane-embedded helix. This loop is critical for catalysis and binding of ligands, especially the lipid-linked sugar moiety [[cite:PUB00098068]]. TMTCs transfers mannosyl residues to the hydroxyl group of serine or threonine residues. The 4 members of the TMTC family are O-mannosyl-transferases acting primarily on the cadherin superfamily; each member has distinct roles in decorating the cadherin domains with O-linked mannose glycans at specific regions. These proteins also act as O-mannosyl-transferase on other proteins such as PDIA3 [[cite:PUB00098069]].

record.description: This group of 2H-phosphodiesterases comprises a single family typified by the protein mlr3352 from M.loti. Members are also present in various alpha-proteobacteria, Synechocystis, Streptococcus and Chilo iridescent virus. The presence of a member of this predominantly bacterial group in a large eukaryotic DNA virus represents a potential case of horizontal transfer from a bacterial source into a virus. Several proteins of bacterial origin have been noticed in the insect viruses (L.M.Iyer, E.V.Koonin and L.Aravind, unpublished observations and these appear to have been acquired from endo-symbiotic or parasitic bacteria that share the same host cells with the viruses. Presence of 2H proteins in the proteomes of large DNA viruses (e.g. T4 57B protein and the Fowl-pox virus FPV025) may point to some role for these proteins in regulating the viral tRNA metabolism. Each member of this family contains an internal duplication, each of which contains an HXTX motif that defines the family.

record.description: This entry represents a highly conserved 100 residue coiled-coil region which is found in short coiled-coil protein (SCOC) in human and UNC-69 in Caenorhabditis elegans. In human, SCOC is required for autophagosome formation during amino acid starvation. It forms a starvation-sensitive trimeric complex with UVRAG (UV radiation resistance associated gene) and FEZ1 and may regulate ULK1 and Beclin 1 complex activities [[cite:PUB00086016]]. In C. elegans, this small, evolutionarily conserved coiled-coil domain-containing protein, UNC-69, acts as a binding partner of UNC-76. Together they participate in a common genetic pathway necessary for axon extension and cooperate to regulate the size and position of synaptic vesicles in axons. Moreover, both proteins colocalize as puncta in neuronal processes and mutations in UNC-69 preferentially disrupt membrane traffic within axons [[cite:PUB00109243]].

record.description: This bacterial family of proteins shows structural similarity to other pectin lyase families. Although structures from this family align with acetyl-transferases, there is no conservation of catalytic residues found. It is likely that the function is one of cell-adhesion. In PDB:3jx8, it is interesting to note that the sequence of contains several well defined sequence repeats, centred around GSG motifs defining the tight beta turn between the two sheets of the super-helix; there are 8 such repeats in the C-terminal half of the protein, which could be grouped into 4 repeats of two. It seems likely that this family belongs to the superfamily of trimeric auto-transporter adhesins (TAAs), which are important virulence factors in Gram-negative pathogens [[cite:PUB00029784]] [[cite:PUB00051306]]. In the case of Parabacteroides distasonis, which is a component of the normal distal human gut microbiota, TAA-like complexes probably modulate adherence to the host (information derived from TOPSAN).
record.name: Putative auto-transporter adhesin, head GIN domain

record.description: This bacterial family of proteins has no known function. However, the cis-regulatory yjdF motif, just upstream from the gene encoding the proteins for this family, is a small non-coding RNA, Rfam:RF01764. The yjdF motif is found in many Firmicutes, including Bacillus subtilis. In most cases, it resides in potential 5' UTRs of homologues of the yjdF gene whose function is unknown. However, in Streptococcus thermophilus, a yjdF RNA motif is associated with an operon whose protein products synthesise nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+). Also, the S. thermophilus yjdF RNA lacks typical yjdF motif consensus features downstream of and including the P4 stem. Thus, if yjdF RNAs are riboswitch aptamers, the S. thermophilus RNAs might sense a distinct compound that structurally resembles the ligand bound by other yjdF RNAs. On the ohter hand, perhaps these RNAs have an alternative solution forming a similar binding site, as is observed with some SAM riboswitches [[cite:PUB00109804]].

record.description: This is a bacterial family of putative lipoproteins. The structure for [swissprot:Q64U78], PDB:3fzx, the first structural template for this large family including several homologues in the human gut microbiome and in metagenomic datasets, folds into a beta barrel that topologically looks like a small-scale porin (such as FepA). [swissprot:Q64U78] is a putative exported protein, and this fold is of the YmcC-like type, with a predicted signal peptide SpI cleavage site AGAMA|QNQDC, and a Phobius server prediction of non-cytoplasmic localisation for amino acids 21-236. The possibility of it being a membrane protein can be ruled out by the hydrophilic nature of the solvent exposed surface outside the barrels. Analysis of sequence conservation suggests that an area near Glu172/Trp206 is potentially interesting. These two residues are also conserved in Dali hit PDB:2in5, a hypothetical lipoprotein classified as a new YmcC-like fold in SCOP (SCOP:159271, with a 12-stranded meander beta-sheet folded into a deformed beta-barrel) despite large structural differences between the two structures, suggesting similarity in function.

record.description: This family of proteins, found from plants to humans, is PRAT4 (A and B), a Protein Associated with Toll-like receptor 4. TLR4 recognizes lipopolysaccharide (LPS), one of the most immuno-stimulatory glycolipids constituting the outer membrane of the Gram-negative bacteria. This family has also been described as a SAP-like MIR-interacting protein family.

record.description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and includes YfiR from E. coli. YfiR has been shown to regulate YfiN, a diguanylate cyclase and a bifunctional protein that produces c-di-GMP in response to reductive stress and then dynamically relocates to the division site to arrest cell division in response to envelope stress in Escherichia coli. YfiR may serve as a periplasmic redox sensor that regulates YfiN activity in response to reducing conditions [[cite:PUB00088310],[cite:PUB00088309]]. HmsC in Yersinia Pestis is the orthologue of YfiR from E. coli [[cite:PUB00091013]]. HmsC is a periplasmic protein that interacts directly with the periplasmic domain (PD) of HmsD and causes proteolytic degradation of HmsD, which in turn negatively regulates Y. pestis biofilm formation [[cite:PUB00091014]].
record.name: YfiR/HmsC-like

record.description: This domain of unknown function has an enolase N-terminal domain-like fold. Its genomic context suggests that it may have a role in anaerobic vitamin B12 biosynthesis. This domain is often found at the N-terminus of proteins containing DUF364, [pfam:PF04016]. The structure of UnioProtKB:B8FUJ5, PDB:3l5o, suggests that the whole protein has this enolase N-terminal-like fold and an Rossmann-like C-terminal domain. Structural and bioinformatic analyses reveal partial similarities to Rossmann-like methyltransferases, with residues from the enolase-like fold combining to form a unique active site that is likely to be involved in the condensation or hydrolysis of molecules implicated in the synthesis of flavins, pterins or other siderophores. The protein may be playing a role in heavy-metal chelation [[cite:PUB00075371]].

record.description: This is a family of unknown function. Family members are found in Bacteria and Eukaryotes. In algae, this family is found on the N-terminal of diphthamide synthase family [pfam:PF01902] and is predicted to be a membrane transporter belonging to The ATP-binding Cassette (ABC) family [[cite:PUB00091274]]. In nematoda, it is found on the N-terminal side of ribosomal protein family L14 [pfam:PF00238]. It is also found on the N-terminal of Cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase [pfam:PF01923] in other eukaryotes. Family members found in homo sapiens such as [swissprot:Q5VUE5], have been shown to be highly expressed in 15 high-grade neuroendocrine tumor cell lines and YAP1-positive small-cell lung cancer cell lines [[cite:PUB00091275]] as well as being up-regulated in two human Multiple Myloma cell lines in response to selective nuclear export inhibitor KPT-276 [[cite:PUB00091276]]. The HMM profile of this family reveals 4 highly conserved cysteines.

record.description: This domain was first discovered in BPSL1050, a highly immunoreactive protein found in Burkholderia pseudomallei. The domain's structure consists of three helical regions which pack onto an antiparallel beta sheet, formed by four strands. The beta sheet is solvent exposed on one side and packs tightly against the three helices on the other side, generating a network of hydrophobic and aromatic interactions that contribute to tight packing of the protein. Is is thought that the small loop L1, the main loop L2, and part of helix alpha-3 extending until Leu120 are the three main immunogenic sequences [[cite:PUB00091370]].

record.description: This family represents a domain of unknown function located between the Transcription factor IIIC subunit delta N-term ([pfam:PF12657]) and the Putative zinc-finger of transcription factor IIIC complex ([pfam:PF12660]) within the transcription Factor IIIC 90 kDa subunit (TFIIIC-delta/TFIIIC90, also known as general transcription factor 3C polypeptide 4). record.description: This entry represents a conserved domain found at the C-terminus of S41 family carboxyl-terminal processing peptidases in members of the phylum Bacteroidota. S41 family peptidases are serine proteases involved in C-terminal processing of proteins, including the removal of C-terminal extensions from penicillin-binding proteins and other substrates. This C-terminal domain is found exclusively in Bacteroidota, particularly in the classes Bacteroidia, Flavobacteriia, Cytophagia and Sphingobacteriia, suggesting it may confer phylum-specific functionality or substrate specificity. The domain architecture of these proteins typically consists of an N-terminal CtpB_N-like domain ([pfam:PF22694]), one or more PDZ domains ([pfam:PF00595], [pfam:PF13180], [pfam:PF17820]), the catalytic Peptidase_S41 domain, and this C-terminal domain. record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8808)

record.description: This entry represents a small helical hairpin domain found at the C-terminus of bacterial signalling proteins. It may form homodimers to make a four helical bundle structure.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8809)

record.description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 110 residues found in Type IIG restriction-modification enzymes in bacteria. This domain is located C-terminal to the TaqI_C domain ([pfam:PF12950]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8810)

record.description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 220 residues found in subtilisin-like serine peptidases in Actinomycetota. This domain is typically located C-terminal to the Peptidase_S8 catalytic domain ([pfam:PF00082]) and PA domain ([pfam:PF02225]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8811)

record.description: This domain of unknown function is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins. Some members are annotated as related to antimicrobial activity. It contains two highly conserved motifs RGYD and RGDY.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8812)

record.description: This entry represents a small C-terminal helical domain of approximately 40 residues found in bacterial ImmA/IrrE family metallopeptidases. This domain is located C-terminal to the Peptidase_M78 catalytic domain ([pfam:PF06114]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8813)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 140 residues found in secreted proteins in Actinomycetota, particularly Pseudonocardiaceae. This domain adopts a double psi beta barrel fold. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8814)

record.description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 125 residues found in multi-domain proteins that contain the DUF7408 domain ([pfam:PF24157]). Structural similarity searches identify this as a member of the galactose-binding domain-like superfamily. This family is found in Bacillota, particularly Bacillales (including Paenibacillus and Bacillaceae) and Clostridia, as well as some Chloroflexota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8815)

record.description: This entry represents a bacterial immunoglobulin-like domain of approximately 65 residues. This domain is found predominantly in Planctomycetota and Bacillota. These domains are typically found in large secreted or surface-associated proteins, often with multiple tandem repeats. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8816)

record.description: This is a family of fungal uncharacterised sequences of unknown function. Some members are annotated as related to antimicrobial resistance. There are two highly conserved motifs FYxxLGF and GxPR.
record.name: Family of unknown function (DUF8817)

record.description: This entry represents a small beta sandwich domain of approximately 82 residues found in large outer membrane proteins in Bacteroidota (Flavobacteriaceae, Cytophagales). The domain is inserted within larger beta-barrel structures. These proteins are associated with the type IX secretion system (T9SS). The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8818)

record.description: This family represents small uncharacterized proteins of approximately 108 residues found in Actinomycetes, particularly Streptomyces and Nocardioides. These proteins typically consist of this single domain only. STRING network analysis shows strong functional association with SIS domains ([pfam:PF01380]) and HTH_6 transcription factors ([pfam:PF01418]), suggesting a possible role in sugar metabolism regulation.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8819)

record.description: This family represents a small domain of approximately 93 amino acids found predominantly in Actinobacteria including Streptomyces, Thermomonosporaceae, and Streptosporangiaceae. The domain is also found in some cyanobacteria. The domain is typically found as the sole domain in uncharacterized proteins and shows genomic context association with DUF6745 domain proteins.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8820)

record.description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins of approximately 145 residues found in Bacillota (particularly Paenibacillaceae and Bacillaceae) and Actinomycetota (including Streptomycetaceae). The proteins occur as single-domain proteins. While computationally annotated as phage tail proteins in UniProt, there is no experimental evidence supporting this function, and the annotation likely reflects genomic proximity to prophage regions rather than demonstrated function. The function of this family remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8821)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 101 residues found in uncharacterized proteins in plants (Viridiplantae) and cyanobacteria. In plants, it is found predominantly in eudicotyledons and monocots. These are small single-domain proteins whose function is unknown.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8822)

record.description: This entry represents a C-terminal globular domain of approximately 110 residues found in large integral membrane proteins from Actinomycetota, particularly Streptomycetaceae (Streptomyces and related genera). The parent proteins are approximately 500-700 residues in length with this domain positioned at the C-terminus. While the proteins are annotated as membrane transporters, the specific function of this C-terminal domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8823)

record.description: This domain of unknown function is found mainly in proteins from Bacillota lineage. It is found C-terminal to a lipoprotein lipid attachment site suggesting that it may be associated with the membrane.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8824)

record.description: This entry represents a small domain of approximately 95 residues found as a single-domain protein in Streptomycetaceae. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain if unknown function (DUF8825)

record.description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 57 residues found in aspartic peptidases in Arachis (peanut). This domain is located C-terminal to the Asp_protease_2 domain ([pfam:PF13650]). These proteins may be associated with transposable elements. The function of this C-terminal domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8826)

record.description: This entry represents a membrane protein domain of approximately 70 residues found in Streptomyces and related Actinomycetes. In Streptomyces coelicolor, SCO4131 containing this domain is located in a gene cluster (SCO4126-SCO4131) that affects actinorhodin antibiotic biosynthesis [[cite:PUB00163737]]. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8827)

record.description: This entry represents a small domain of approximately 70 residues found in uncharacterized proteins in Bacteroidota, predominantly Flavobacteriaceae. These are small single-domain proteins. Some entries are annotated as 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase, but this annotation appears to be erroneous given the small size and lack of typical dehydrogenase features.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8828)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 110 residues found in small uncharacterized proteins in Streptomyces and related Actinomycetes. These proteins typically consist of this single domain only. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8829)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 100 residues found in small uncharacterized proteins in Streptomyces and related Actinomycetes. These proteins typically consist of this single domain only. Foldseek analysis suggests weak structural similarity to DUF6204 ([pfam:PF19707]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8830)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 62 residues found in small uncharacterized proteins in Alphaproteobacteria, particularly Rhodobacterales (Roseobacteraceae, Paracoccaceae). These proteins typically consist of this single domain only. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8831)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 110 residues found in uncharacterised proteins in bacteria, predominantly in Actinomycetes (Streptomyces, Micromonospora) and some Bacilli. This domain adopts an immunoglobulin-like fold and is a member of clan CL0159. Many proteins contain two tandem copies of this domain. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8832)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 60 amino acids found at the N-terminal of 20.7 kDa protein in NOF-FB from Drosophila melanogaster and as tandem arrays of 10-11 copies in other members of this entry, from insects. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8833)

record.description: This entry represents a small domain of approximately 43 residues found in uncharacterized proteins in Streptomycetaceae. The STRING analysis indicates functional association with hydrolase domains ([pfam:PF00561], PF12146, PF12697). This domain is predicted to adopt a simple structure composed of three-stranded beta-sheet and an alpha-helix. The function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8834)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 160 residues found in uncharcaterised proteins from Proteobacteria.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8835)

record.description: This entry represents a small domain of approximately 65 amino acids found in Actinomycetes. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich structure composed of two three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheets packed on each other.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8836)

record.description: This domain of unknown function is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly found in firmicutes. This domain is predicted to adopt a mainly beta structure. It shows highly conserved motifs TAY and VxDxG.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8837)

record.description: This domain is found C-terminal in bacterial proteins containing at the N terminus a methyltransferase domain.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8838)

record.description: This entry represents a family of small proteins of approximately 50 residues found in Actinomycetes, predominantly in Streptomyces. The function of this family remains to be determined. Members are predicted to fold into a simple structure composed of a small three stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and an alpha-helix connecting the first and the second beta-strand.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8839)

record.description: This entry represents a family of small proteins of approximately 110 residues found predominantly in Bacteroidota, particularly Flavobacteriaceae. The function of this family remains to be determined. Members are predicted to adopt a structure with significant similarity to members of the PDDEXK superfamily and in particular to [pfam:PF02021].
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8840)

record.description: This entry represents a domain found in probable transcriptional regulators from Actinomycetota predominantly in the genus Streptomyces. These proteins contain an N-terminal helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain followed by this domain. The function of this domain is unknown.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8841)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function frequently found C-terminal in proteins from Actinomycetota. This domain is distantly related to [pfam:PF19374] (DUF5949). The gene SCO1756 encoding a protein with this domain was found to be more abundant in bacterioferritin mutants during morphological differentiation [[cite:PUB00163738]], although the specific function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8842)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 120 residues found in uncharacterized proteins in Ascomycota fungi, including Sordariomycetes (Fusarium, Nectriaceae), Eurotiomycetes (Aspergillus), and Dothideomycetes. The function of this domain is unknown.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8843)

record.description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins from Actinomycetes. STRING analysis indicates functional association with His_Phos_1 ([pfam:PF00300]) and AAA ATPase domains.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8844)

record.description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins from Bacteroidota, particularly in Flavobacteriaceae. These proteins are approximately 200 amino acids in length and are predicted to be membrane-associated. STRING analysis shows these proteins are functionally associated with sigma-70 factors ([pfam:PF04542] and [pfam:PF08281]) and other regulatory proteins. The function of this protein family remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8845)

record.description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in uncharcaterised proteins from Alphaproteobacteria, predominantly in Rhodobacterales (including Roseobacteraceae and Paracoccaceae). The domain is approximately 100 residues in length and is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure containing a four stranded antiparallel beta-sheet. STRING analysis shows these proteins are consistently associated with cell division and secretion system proteins, including DivIB ([pfam:PF03799]), RodZ ([pfam:PF13464]) and SPOR domain proteins ([pfam:PF05036]). The specific function of this domain remains to be determined.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8846)

record.description: This family represents a small domain of approximately 69 amino acids found in uncharacterised proteins from Actinobacteria, particularly Streptomyces, Micromonospora, and Pseudonocardiaceae. It contains a conserved FxGGpxDG sequence motif. This domain is predicted to fold into an open five-stranded beta-barrel.
record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8847)

record.description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised plant proteins that are predicted to mainly adopt a disordered fold. They are rich in G residues.
record.name: Family of unknown function (DUF8848)

record.description: This family represents a group of uncharacterised proteins predominantly found in echinoderms. Members are predicted to show an alpha configuration. They have several highly conserved motifs EE and highly conserved residues K, Q, W and H.
record.name: Family of unknown function (DUF8849)

top_by_proteins.description: The function of this family is unknown.
top_by_proteins.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF397)

top_by_proteins.description: This entry represents a putative ligand binding domain found in bacterial transcription regulators that have an N-terminal HTH domain [pfam:PF13560].
top_by_proteins.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF5753)

top_by_proteins.description: This family of prokaryotic proteins have no known function. [swissprot:P71138] a protein of unknown function in the family has been misannotated as alpha-dextrin 6-glucanohydrolase.
top_by_proteins.name: Protein of unknown function DUF58

top_by_proteins.description: This domain contains several highly conserved charged amino acids, suggesting this may be an enzymatic domain (Bateman A pers. obs). The entry includes SanA [swissprot:P33017] and Sfix ([swissprot:O33790]) from Salmonella typhimurium which are involved in Vancomycin resistance [[cite:PUB00019464]]. These proteins may be involved in murein synthesis [[cite:PUB00019465]]. This domain is found in Escherichia coli YdcF, which has been shown to bind S-adenosyl-L-methionine (AdoMet), but whose biochemical function has not been identified [[cite:PUB00050945]].
top_by_proteins.name: DUF218 domain

top_by_proteins.description: This domain is found at the C terminus of the YchF GTP-binding protein ([swissprot:O13998]) and is possibly related to the ubiquitin-like and MoaD/ThiS superfamilies.
top_by_proteins.name: Protein of unknown function (DUF933)

top_by_proteins.description: This domain family is found in plants, and is approximately 100 amino acids in length. Considering the very diverse range of other domains it is associated with it is possible that this domain is a binding/guiding region. There are two highly conserved tryptophan residues.
top_by_proteins.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4283)

top_by_proteins.description: This entry (ex DUF4371) represents a RNase-like domain in Zinc finger MYM-type protein 1 (ZMYM1), FAM200 and similar proteins mainly found in animals. FAM200 is characterised by its involvement in cellular regulatory processes, its precise function remains to be elucidated.
top_by_proteins.name: ZMYM1/FAM200, RNase-like domain

top_by_proteins.description: The function of the plant proteins constituting this family is unknown.
top_by_proteins.name: Plant protein of unknown function

top_by_proteins.description: This is a family of proteins of unknown function. Most of the members are gag-polyproteins.
top_by_proteins.name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1759)

top_by_proteins.description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes, including NTF2-Like SgcJ protein from Streptomyces carzinostaticus, which plays a role in the biosynthesis of the 9-membered enediyne antitumor antibiotic C-1027. It shows a cone-like alpha+beta barrel structure with a long N-terminal alpha- helix, a curved six-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and two additional shorter alpha-helices. Its specific function is still unkown [[cite:PUB00100883]].
top_by_proteins.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4440)

top_by_proteins.description: This presumed domain is found in a range of retrotransposon polyproteins.
top_by_proteins.name: Family of unknown function (DUF5641)

top_by_proteins.description: This family consists of hypothetical proteins some of which are putative membrane proteins. No functional information or experimental verification of function is known. This domain is around 100 amino acids long.
top_by_proteins.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF202)

top_by_proteins.description: This family includes the DUF34/metal-binding protein/NIF3 proteins, which are widely distributed across superkingdoms. They were previously annotated as GTP cyclohydrolase 1 type 2 [[cite:PUB00070175]] and, recently, through a comprehensive literature review and integrative bioinformatics analyses it was revealed that annotations for these members were misleading as they were based on a single set of in vitro results examining the NIF3 homolog of Helicobacter pylori [[cite:PUB00070175]]. Actually, they have varied phenotypes with the unifying functional role as metal-binding proteins [[cite:PUB00100327]]. This entry contains several NIF3 (NGG1p interacting factor 3) protein homologues. NIF3 interacts with the yeast transcriptional coactivator NGG1p which is part of the ADA complex, the exact function of this interaction is unknown [[cite:PUB00002954],[cite:PUB00019927]].
top_by_proteins.name: Duf34/NIF3 (NGG1p interacting factor 3)

top_by_proteins.description: This family is often found associated to the N-terminus of the HNH endonuclease domain [pfam:PF01844]. The function of this domain is uncertain. This family has been called the 13E12 repeat family [[cite:PUB00057273]].
top_by_proteins.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF222)

top_by_proteins.description: This domain is found in the Intracellular iron chaperone frataxin YdhG [[cite:PUB00098100]] and the uncharacterised protein YdeI from Bacillus subtilis.
top_by_proteins.name: Domain of unknown function (DU1801)

top_by_proteins.description: This presumed domain is found at the N-terminus of many proteins found in transposons.
top_by_proteins.name: Transposase domain (DUF772)

top_by_proteins.description: This entry represents a large family of fungal integral membrane proteins.
top_by_proteins.name: Family of unknown function (DUF6534)

top_by_proteins.description: This presumed domain is found at the C-terminus of bacterial RNA polymerase ECF sigma factor proteins.
top_by_proteins.name: Family of unknown function (DUF6596)

top_by_proteins.description: Members of this family have so far been found in bacteria and mouse SwissProt or TrEMBL entries. However possible family members have also been identified in translated rat (Genbank:AW144450) and human (Genbank:AI478629) ESTs. A mouse family member has been named SIMPL (signalling molecule that associates with mouse pelle-like kinase). SIMPL appears to facilitate and/or regulate complex formation between IRAK/mPLK (IL-1 receptor-associated kinase) and IKK (inhibitor of kappa-B kinase) containing complexes, and thus regulate NF-kappa-B activity [[cite:PUB00010115]]. Separate experiments demonstrate that a mouse family member (named LaXp180) binds the Listeria monocytogenes surface protein ActA, which is a virulence factor that induces actin polymerisation. It may also bind stathmin, a protein involved in signal transduction and in the regulation of microtubule dynamics [[cite:PUB00009982]]. In bacteria its function is unknown, but it is thought to be located in the periplasm or outer membrane.
top_by_proteins.name: Protein of unknown function (DUF541)
